column3: The Hebrew says “beyond the Jordan”; BSB specifies “east of the Jordan.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says that Moses “spoke” to the sons of Israel; BSB uses “proclaimed.”

“The Amorite” is a collective singular in Hebrew. BSB separates Edrei as the place of defeating Og, whereas the Hebrew leaves the location attached to the following wording without a second verb of defeating.
The Hebrew says “beyond the Jordan”; BSB makes the eastern side explicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins with “turn” and “set out,” and uses collective singulars for “the Amorite” and “the Canaanite.” It repeats “river” before Euphrates.
“Their seed” is singular and collective in Hebrew; BSB uses “their descendants.”
The Hebrew says “carry you”; BSB expands this to “carry the burden for you.”
The Hebrew links the clauses with “and behold,” rather than “so that.”
The Hebrew says “as He spoke to you”; BSB interprets the speaking as a promise.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the men “known”; BSB interprets this as “respected.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “leaders” before each numerical group and calls the men “known,” rather than “respected.”
The Hebrew repeats “between” and says “his foreign resident,” while BSB supplies “disputes” and uses “or.”
The Hebrew uses the images of recognizing faces and fearing a man’s face; BSB renders their sense as partiality and intimidation.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew reports arrival at Kadesh-barnea as a completed clause; BSB turns it into the introduction “When we reached.” “The Amorite” is a collective singular.
“The Amorite” is a collective singular in Hebrew; BSB uses “the Amorites.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the matter was “good in my eyes”; BSB renders the image as “seemed good to me.”
The Hebrew says “they turned” and uses a word for a stream or wadi; BSB has “They left” and “Valley.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “the mouth of the LORD”; BSB renders the image as His command.
“The Amorite” is a collective singular. The Hebrew says “to destroy us,” while BSB uses the passive “to be annihilated.”
The Hebrew asks where they are “going up,” uses singular “our heart,” and says the cities are “fortified in the heavens”; BSB supplies “walls.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says “before your eyes”; BSB renders this as “just as you saw Him do.”
